newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court blocks EU funding for social programmes.
newsitem.headline: Court blocks EU funding for social programmes.

text.p: The European Court of Justice, responding to bids from Britain and Germany, blocked plans by the European Commission to spend 12 million Ecus for pilot social projects for the poor and elderly.

London, supported by Bonn, argued that the decision to spend the money -- which was to fund projects such as helping women to quit prostitution and homeless people to join mainstream society -- should have been taken by the Council of Ministers.

The president of the EU court issued an order to suspend the funding pending a final ruling on Cases 239/96 R and 240/96 R. "It is not possible at the present stage to rule out the possibility that the Commission may in fact have acted unlawfully in the place of the Council," he said in a statement.
Britain argued that the Commission, which approved the money in May, was seeking to implement proposals on its own that the Council had earlier rejected.

The Commission allocated the money after Germany vetoed a programme to help older people and joined with Britain to block a programme to combat "social and economic exclusion" in the Social Affairs Council last year.
Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn said in a statement that the case showed that the EU treaty should be amended to allow programmes to be adopted by majority vote rather than unanimity.

"The Commission will of course fully respect the order of the Court," he said. "I understand that this will cause great disappointment to the many (non-governmental organisations) working with the poor and elderly, whose projects it will not be able to fund, at least until the Court issues its final judgment."
The Court said the Commission could make funding commitments if it made them conditional on the final ruling and made no payments before then.
